title: Finite affine section cover in a single positive tensor power
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $L$ an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] ample in the absolute sense [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. There exist $m>0$, $r\ge0$, and global section morphisms $s_i: \mathcal O_X\to L^{\otimes m}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], indexed by $\operatorname{ULift}(\operatorname{Fin}(r+1))$, such that each complement $X_{s_i}$ of the support of its zero locus is affine, and $\bigcup_iX_{s_i}=X$. The zero locus is the locally principal ideal generated by the coefficient of $s_i$ in a rank-one trivialization.

source.place: Morphisms Lemma 01VS, first paragraph (finite affine section cover, degrees made common); Properties Definition 01PS, with the local rank-one description of nonvanishing.

proof.text: Unpack IsAmple and choose an affine section locus through each point. Use the proved section-nonvanishing-zero-locus comparison to express it as the complement of Hom.zeroLocus support. IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover gives a finite set t of points whose chosen loci cover X.

Use the finite nonempty index type Option t, adding the zero section in degree one at none. Hom.zeroLocus_eq_bot_iff and IdealSheafData.support_bot show its open is bottom, hence affine. The some entries retain the chosen affine opens and cover. Take m=product of their degrees d(i); all d(i)>0, so m>0 and d(i) divides m. Quotients m/d(i) are positive. tensorPowSection and tensorPowMulIso followed by the equality d(i)*(m/d(i))=m produce common-degree sections. Hom.zeroLocus_eq_of_arrowIso and the source lemma compl_support_zeroLocus_tensorPowSection identify their open loci with the original ones.

The finite type Option t is nonempty even when X is empty. Enumerate it using Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq and Equiv.ulift as ULift(Fin(r+1)). Reindex the affine-locus assertions; surjectivity of this equivalence preserves the supremum of the opens, so it remains top.
